items.summary: 近日行业观察人士Satvat表示，任天堂、卡普空和科乐美等日本游戏公司保持了相对健康的经营状态。这些企业的员工留任率均超过97%，规模较小的开发团队及相对克制的高管薪酬，被认为是重要原因。 Satvat称日本开发团队通常

content.v: 近日行业观察人士Satvat表示，任天堂、卡普空和科乐美等日本游戏公司保持了相对健康的经营状态。这些企业的员工留任率均超过97%，规模较小的开发团队及相对克制的高管薪酬，被认为是重要原因。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260918/1789678847_392934_jpg_r.jpg
Satvat称日本开发团队通常更小、更精简，没有大规模追随服务型游戏趋势，也较少组建人数达到500人的大型项目团队。与北美和欧洲同行相比，这种人员结构使相关公司较少出现频繁裁员。
其统计显示，2026年至今，北美占全球游戏行业裁员事件的66%，涉及人数占79%；北美与欧洲合计占全部裁员事件的96%。Satvat还估计，此前一段持续12至18个月的时期内，全球超过半数的行业裁员发生在美国加利福尼亚州。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260918/1789678848_318144_jpg_r.jpg
Satvat认为，对于身处北美或西欧传统3A级工作室的开发者而言，当前冲击可与1983年的行业危机相比。他将这些地区称为本轮行业动荡中受破坏最严重的区域，而日本游戏行业呈现出不同状况。
高管薪酬差异也是其观察重点。材料列举的数据显示，EA负责人Andrew Wilson上一财年的薪酬为3864.9984万美元，约为该公司员工薪酬中位数的305倍；任天堂同期披露的社长古川俊太郎总薪酬约为200万美元。
按照Satvat的预测，2022年至2026年间，游戏行业共削减57628个岗位，但同期新增岗位数量与之相当。经历大规模岗位调整后，行业从业总人数仍实现小幅增长，净增人数为数千人。

items.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker sequel may not have the divisive time mechanic that so many players dislike: 'We will not force it,' game director says
items.summary: Konrad Tomaszkiewicz says players can use mods if they don't like Dawnwalkers ticking clock, but he encourages

others.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker’s Hunger Is a Dark Urge to Match Baldur’s Gate 3

content.v: The Blood of Dawnwalker is a pretty excellent RPG, but there's one aspect of it that not everyone loves: Time. Simply put, it's a limited resource in the game, which restricts what Coen—that's you—can do. Our reviewer, Australian editor Shaun Prescott, found it injected a sense of urgency into the game , at least in the early going, but said he'd "also like to pick some nirnroot and play some Gwent, thank you very much"—that is, have the time to relax and fiddle with non-essential tasks on his own terms, at his own pace.

Other players clearly felt the same way: One of the first mods to come out for The Blood of Dawnwalker is the " Better Story Timer ," which effectively eliminates the impact of the ticking clock entirely—and which has since become, by far, the most popular Dawnwalker mod on Nexus Mods.

How much of an impact that reaction has had over at developer Rebel Wolves is impossible to say, but in an interview with Eurogamer , studio CEO and game director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz said it might not be used for the game's sequel.

"We will play with it. If we will have parts of the story, or the whole story, to which it fits, then we will use it," Tomaszkiewicz said. "If we will have stories where it does not fit, we will not force it. We will play with this system and we will try to use it to boost the urgency of some events in the game. But I'm not saying that in every game we will have the same scheme or loop—it's not like this."

Tomaszkiewicz acknowledged complaints about the time mechanic, and the mods available to remove it. He doesn't have a problem with that, but he does encourage players to try Dawnwalker with the clock running first: "We balanced [Dawnwalker] in a way that it's possible to do around 80 percent of the content with the time mechanic so it's not so bad.

"The arguments of, 'I want to see everything in one playthrough,' I understand, but it's false to begin with, because even in games like The Witcher, you cannot see everything in one playthrough because you have choices and consequences, and different things happen when you choose different things," Tomaszkiewicz said.

I have that same feeling myself with most games—I want to see everything the first time—but Tomaszkiewicz is correct: The Witcher 2 forces players to make a choice at a critical juncture that unavoidably excludes a significant amount of gameplay, and that seemed fine; Obsidian's Pentiment , released to acclaim in 2022, has a very strict time mechanic of its own that's essential to the experience. Missing out on things in videogames is not all that new or unusual—if anything, it's the inevitable outcome of choice in videogames that so many players say they want.

Interestingly, Tomaszkiewicz said that complaints about the time mechanic have tailed off considerably now that Dawnwalker has been out for a couple weeks, because people have finished the game and realized they actually had more time than they needed—a pattern he expects to continue as players continue to wrap it up.

"There will always be people who will have a problem with that because they don't like time mechanics at all, but I think that is fine," he said. "They can download the mod and play without it if they want."

And yes, even though The Blood of Dawnwalker has only been out for a couple weeks, Rebel Wolves is already eyeballing a sequel: The studio is now looking for a lead writer to help "craft the next chapter in the Dawnwalker saga."

content.v: Take-Two确认，《GTAOL》不会随着《GTA6》发售而结束。公司计划在新作推出后继续为现有在线模式提供支持。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260918/1789678622_572291.jpg
Take-Two在近期股东会议上表示：“我们将在《GTA6》发售后及更长时间内继续支持《GTAOL》。”这意味着新作面世后，玩家仍可继续使用目前的在线模式。
Rockstar Games此前已经确认，《GTA6》发售时仅包含单人游戏，不会同步推出多人模式。至于新一代在线模式将于何时推出、是否作为本体后续内容加入，或采用独立发行方式，目前均未公布。
Twitch负责人丹·克兰西认为，《GTA6》的多人内容可能在2027年推出。他表示，自己曾与Rockstar讨论其后续计划以及创作者参与方式。不过，Take-Two与Rockstar尚未正式确认这一时间。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260914/1789339255_585453_jpg_r.jpg
股东会议还谈及了PC平台。Take-Two首席执行官施特劳斯·泽尔尼克表示，公司通常会逐步面向拥有可观用户群的平台推出作品，PC平台对公司的重要性也在持续上升，但他没有确认《GTA6》PC版的具体安排。
Rockstar过去通常先推出主机版本，PC版随后跟进。前Rockstar制作人约翰·里奇奥此前称，这种安排源于团队希望先围绕主机性能完成优化，再将游戏扩展至PC平台。目前《GTA6》计划于11月19日发售，现有《GTAOL》则将在此后继续获得支持。

items.title: Brandon Sanderson Says He 'Would Love to' Create Tabletop Adaptations of His Cytoverse Books

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/05/21/81ualu6laol-sl1500-1-1779379333131.jpg

Brandon Sanderson has been heavily invested in making tabletop adaptations of his Cosmere books . Most recently, he's been collaborating with Brotherwise Games on standalone board games as well as a larger Cosmere TTRPG. It's unsurprising, then, that his interest in such adaptations expands beyond his most popular literary universe.
IGN recently had the chance to interview Sanderson , and we asked him if he's considered making tabletop adaptations of Skyward and the rest of the Cytoverse.

"I would love to! We've talked about it. However, I also want to be aware of asking my fans for too much," Sanderson told IGN. "There are a lot of great books out there, and a lot of great games. I don't want or need it to be all Brandon Sanderson all the time. We try to be very deliberate and careful about these kinds of collaborations, to only be doing what will feel the most exciting to my fans."

Sanderson's answer here doesn't rule out the possibility of a Cytoverse tabletop adaptation, but it certainly indicates that it won't be happening any time soon. The release of Blightfall marks the first official book expansion into the Cytoverse, and it was recently revealed that a Skyward TV series is in the works.

While Sanderson's YA sci-fi series isn't nearly as popular as The Cosmere, it definitely has potential to grow in the future. If the Skyward TV series is able to find success on streaming , it seems inevitable that some sort of tabletop collab would follow. That being said, we're still looking at a long wait before that TV adaptation actually happens. The Mistborn movie, for example, is looking at a release date of 2031 or later , and that's further along than the Skyward series.

Despite no future plans for tabletop adaptations for the Cytoverse, Sanderson still has some exciting upcoming projects in the works with Brotherwise. The Cosmere RPG is officially getting its Mistborn expansion in November , and a massive War for Roshar strategy game is also in the works. If you're a fan of Sanderson's books and tabletop games, there's a lot of great stuff coming your way.

items.title: Wardogs is the only FPS where I actually expect to get revived
items.summary: Bribe or no bribe, people want to help in Wardogs.

content.v: There exists in classed-based military shooters an understanding: Never count on a random medic to care about you.

You'd think in games where players have to opt into the support role, it'd be as simple as "There's a medic nearby, they'll try to get me," but any Battlefield player will tell you how often trained doctors trample over their corpse, more hungry to end a life than save one. So you learn to assume that you're on your own, and when a real medic does go out of their way to help you, they're the exception that proves the rule.

Wardogs is different. Help is so abundant in this 100-player, three-team milsim that, when I die, I can be confident a second, third, or even a fourth chance is coming. It's the only FPS I've played where multiple medics will actually race to give me first-aid, drag my body to safety, or pop a smoke grenade to cover a revive.

I've also played shooters where support play is taken more seriously than in Battlefield—Squad, Hell Let Loose, Isonzo, Arma, and other games on the "milsim" spectrum come to mind—but Bulkhead has successfully crafted a medic role so accessible and appealing that damn near everyone in Wardogs wants to help. Official stats from Wardogs' first weekend reveal that players earned 123 million kills and 61 million revives for an overall resurrection rate of nearly 50%. As a lifelong medic main, that's astounding.
How does Wardogs do it? I think a lot of factors contribute:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/wPscF8gnGvw5VsasbakPSX-1920-80.jpg
Money, obviously

The big one is Wardogs' unique, cash-infused incentive structure. Unlike an extraction shooter, where money is earned primarily through kills and selling valuable loot, Wardogs will make you rich just for doing useful, nonviolent things for the team: killing, capturing, transporting, spotting, building, and healing .

On top of the fuzzy feelings I get for helping out, Medic is a very profitable playstyle in Wardogs. A single revive pays almost as much as a kill, and that's before you factor in tips from grateful patients and automatic assist payouts when those patients go on to get more kills. If I go the extra mile of buying spare bandages to heal folks back to 100, I get even more cash and tips.

Battlefield 6 also showers dedicated medics with XP, and really good ones end up near the top of the scoreboard, but Wardogs' cash prizes feel more impactful because it's the currency that fuels everything you do. Going on a 50k profit run in a single life can mean I've taken a big step toward unlocking an expensive upgrade, or it can mean that I get to splurge on my next loadout with a bigger backpack or vehicle. It's smart stuff.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/us5fp2T3dBfxeTX3ReU4YB-1920-80.jpg
Anyone can revive

You don't have to invest in medic gear to lend a hand. Anyone can drag bodies and revive friendlies, and the vendor gives away a single-use quick-revive tool once per life. There's a world where this design choice could've been controversial in Wardogs, because if anyone can revive, what do you need proper medics for? But Bulkhead has threaded the needle perfectly by making manual "hand" revives—where your soldier literally rubs their hands together for ~20 seconds like they're charging defibrillators paddles—extremely slow.

Teammates can and will try to save you this way, but the speed and efficiency of upgrading to proper defibrillators (unlocked at medic level 11) is dramatic. A kitted-up medic can have a full squad back on its feet in the same time as a single hand revive. And even though there are no enforced classes in Wardogs, defibs are expensive and take up your one "specialist" tool slot that could hold an RPG or binoculars instead. This ensures that anyone can heal, but not everyone can be a proper medic.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/A7949vS7ugHa7t2NhzR2fE-1920-80.jpg
It's not that dangerous to be a medic

I have found that going for a revive in Wardogs is not as risky as in similar games. Often (but not always) when I sprint toward a dead body out in the open, I'm able to drag them behind cover without drama.

I suspect this has to do with how spread out the action is in Wardogs: a three-team structure means there's no singular front where all of the death happens, which also means there's not a single pile of dead bodies that enemies are staring at, waiting for medics to make a move. No, most of my Wardogs skirmishes have been smaller in scale—confrontations with two or three clustered enemies or a showdown with a single sniper I can't even see.

It's a stark contrast to Battlefield 6, where some maps are so congested (and the time-to-kill so short) that the three seconds it takes to equip defibs and use them is enough for someone to sprint around a corner and shoot you in the face. Wardogs' pace is far better suited for support play.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Ex9eaczFQNY7o4AdbvL3im-1920-80.jpg
Bribing is fun, but not as important as I thought

The bribes help. As Sean highlighted last week the ability to bribe nearby medics up to $500 to pick you up can grease the wheels in desperate scenarios. For the first few days of Wardogs, I'd max out my bribe every time because it was cheaper than losing a whole loadout, but I've noticed lately that many players will attempt a revive regardless because, as we've covered, the base pay for a revive is incentive enough.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/5Gmn6jTZiJrmXygLk6zX2L-1920-80.jpg
Dead players don't give up, because dying costs time and money

Wardogs is unique in its commitment to death costing time. There are no Battlefield-like squad spawns, no rally points, and not even FOBs themselves are respawn beacons. There are only two ways to get back in the action: Use your team's one APC (a mobile respawn vehicle with a long cooldown after use) or hitch a ride for the 3km journey from HQ.

Both options are more expensive, and often significantly slower, than just waiting for a revive. I can't overemphasize how important that is, because it means that dead players choose to be patient and give medics a chance. There's nothing I hate more as a support player than folks giving up on me as I'm trying to stick my neck out for them, but so far in Wardogs, this has happened exactly once.

It's still really early days for Wardogs, and the game itself keeps changing as players unlock increasingly elaborate tools, but I'm impressed with how well its rules, scale, gadgets, and incentives coalesce around cooperation. The medic role might be the best example of that synergy in action.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever players are reliving 2004 with hour-long queue times to get into the highly-anticipated beta
items.summary: Blizzard says it's working on getting everyone in as soon as possible.

content.v: WoW: Forever , Blizzard's modernized twist on WoW Classic, launched a beta today, but most people have only experienced a login screen so far. Following a live Q&A, Blizzard turned the WoW: Forever beta servers on. The queue times weren't too bad to start: I had about a nine-minute wait when I first logged in. But once it finished, I was disconnected and kicked to the back of the line for another, even longer queue. It appears I'm not the only one who has made it past the queue only to be disconnected and prompted to start the whole process over again. Players and streamers are all reporting similar issues, although some people have successfully made it in. Blizzard acknowledged the issues on X : "We're working through some final issues, and we expect the doors to open soon."
Thank you to everyone waiting to get into the WoW: Forever Beta.We're working through some final issues, and we expect the doors to open soon.Thank you for your patience! September 17, 2026

There doesn't seem to be any trick to the queue. You just need to wait it out and pray that it lets you past the initial login screen. WoW: Forever is the first version of WoW that doesn't use realms, or servers, in the same way as the others. Instead of picking a realm, you pick a ruleset (normal, PvP, or Roleplay) and join the same server as everyone else. Blizzard did it this way to help preserve the social aspect of the original MMO. This might also be why the queue times are so rough. Wowhead and others have been busy datamining the game's files for new details. You can already go through all the new class talent trees and peek at some of the reworked armor sets . It might be worth taking a look while you wait to get in, or, if you're like me and don't want to spoil everything, cross your fingers and hope you can play a little before the risk of long queues gets even worse on the weekend. There will be plenty of time to play the WoW: Forever beta, however. It'll stick around until October 21 before Blizzard fixes it up for its November 4 launch.

items.title: Denuvo is on the hunt for DRM cracker 'voices38' as the company attempts to take one of its biggest foes to court
items.summary: Step one: Finding out who "voices38" is.

content.v: As reported by TorrentFreak , the ubiquitous DRM producer, Denuvo, is attempting to take one of its biggest foes to court over their work circumventing the antipiracy measures on games like Hogwarts Legacy and Black Myth: Wukong. The case is unique in that it comes from Denuvo and not one of the individual copyright-holders of an affected game.

The target of the lawsuit, who goes by "voices38" on various channels, is particularly prolific when it comes to putting out DRM-circumventing patches or "cracks" for games that license Denuvo's copy protection software. Denuvo is suing voices38 under the anti-circumvention provisions of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), which prohibits tampering with digital protections.

While voices38 is an anonymous actor, Denuvo lists a number of social and gaming services accounts associated with them in its filing, an indication that the company will likely subpoena Valve, Reddit, and/or Discord for identifying information. We saw a similar move from Rockstar recently as it attempted to uncover the identity of GTA6 leaker Cyberleek.

"On information and belief, Defendant is an individual who has circumvented Denuvo’s technological measures that effectively control access to copyrighted works," Denuvo wrote in its filing with the Northern District of California. "Defendant has further announced, posted, or disclosed online, including through Reddit, how to circumvent Denuvo's technological measures that effectively control access to copyrighted works, facilitating or allowing others to similarly circumvent those controls and access video games without authorization."

Denuvo's software is largely unpopular with gamers, pirates or paying customers, as it is seen as invasive and a drain on system resources ( Denuvo claims that its software does not affect game performance), but major publishers still turn to it as an antipiracy measure. Denuvo's legal strategy echoes the successful actions taken by Bungie and Activision against cheat developers for their competitive multiplayer games⁠. In addition to keeping up in the anticheat arms race, some companies have taken to suing cheat makers out of existence.

But part of what let them pursue that strategy is the fact that developing hacks for multiplayer games had evolved into a grey market business with identifiable, profit-making entities to sue, while piracy is more diffuse and inherently not a moneymaker. Successfully unmasking voices38 is the cornerstone of any successful legal action by Denuvo.

Voices38 does not seem particularly bothered by the threat, or they're just playing it very, very cool. "All is fine, everything will continue as normal," they wrote in a comment on the piracy-focused CrackWatch subreddit.

items.title: Zero Parades: Director's Cut will challenge you to drive a stolen truck through a busy roundabout while stoned out of your mind
items.summary: The Director's Cut is coming as a free update in October.

others.title: Zero Parades Lands on PS5 in Director's Cut Form on 3rd November

content.v: Just four months after the release of Zero Parades: For Dead Spies , and two months after laying off a significant number of employees, Studio ZA/UM has announced Zero Parades: Director's Cut, a major update that will add roughly 40,000 words of new content, a new encounter, and other improvements and fixes.

From the announcement on Steam : "Zero Parades: Director's Cut is the definitive edition of our espionage RPG, bringing more story, scenery and mind-fuckery to discover during your bid to reunite The Whole Sick Crew. And yes, we heard you: that includes more Melita."

All due respect to Melita, but the real centerpiece of the Director's Cut appears to be Quisach Roundabout, a new "dramatic encounter" about escaping the titular roundabout. As someone who lives in a country where roundabouts are still relatively new and rare, I'd say that sounds relatable, but apparently this adventure runs a little deeper than just having to figure out which lane you're supposed to be in.

"Hershel and her old friend Ramses find themselves stoned out of their minds, behind the wheel of a hijacked tuk-tuk and seemingly unable to escape the Quisach Roundabout late at night. The objective seems simple enough: take the right exit and head home. Fail to do so, and well... things might get existential. And possibly fatal."

The Director's Cut also offers a new "backstage mode," providing a look at technical insights into the game's development, cut content, and stories from art director Kaspar Tamsalu, new clothing, interactions, death screens, and "atmospheric additions," various quality of life improvements, "and loads more."

Zero Parades: Director's Cut sounds a lot like Disco Elysium: The Final Cut , which brought full voice acting, new characters, a new location, and more to the acclaimed 2019 RPG. But there's one notable difference: Where The Final Cut arrived a year and a half after Disco Elysium's release, Zero Parades: Director's Cut is dropping just four months after the original release. The relatively muted response to Zero Parades compared to Disco Elysium may be a factor in that seeming rush, particularly given that the studio previously cited that shortcoming as the reason for layoff of up to 32 people that was announced in July.

In any event, the response to the Director's Cut from Zero Parades fans is very positive, and it does represent a second chance of sorts for the game: It's coming as a free update for current owners on October 1, and will also mark the game's launch on PlayStation 5, which is set to happen on November 3.

items.title: Scientists Discovered A New Cat Before Rockstar Could Finish GTA 6
items.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in development since 2015 , and a lot of things have happened since the

content.v: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in development since 2015 , and a lot of things have happened since then, including the recent discovery a new species of cat.

The scientific journal Current Biology disclosed the discovery of Leopardus tilcayo--known as the tilcayo tiger cat--this week. The adorable little creature is smaller than your typical housecat, featuring spots and round ears. According to the discovery, the cat species was found in the Bolivian Yungas forest.
The tilcayo tiger cat is the first new cat species discovered in over 100 years.

Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, a co-author of the report, told NBC News that it is currently unknown how many of the cats remain in the wild. She said she discovered the cat basically by accident. She volunteers at a wildlife rehab facility close to La Paz, Bolivia and noticed a tiny cat that she thought was a kitten.

The cat was brought to the facility by a man who was caring for it, feeding it rice and eggs, and later giving it up when he was unable to care for it. Genetic testing was undertaken, and it was discovered that it was indeed a brand-new species of cat never before discovered or documented.

As for more gaming-related things that have happened since GTA 5 came out, GameSpot recently assembled a collection of some of the biggest news stories, including Halo coming to PlayStation, the release of 15+ Call of Duty games, the entire run of Phil Spencer as Xbox CEO , and more.
The wait for GTA 6 has been so long that it's spawned the, “We got ___ before GTA VI” meme. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said he is aware of these memes. “I’ve seen some of those," he said .

The wait for GTA 6 is nearly over, as the game is scheduled for release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game will not ship on a disc, but if you want a disc with GTA 6 printed on it, you can buy the game's soundtrack .

items.title: Diablo 4's anniversary event brings back the game's most iconic location, and boy that music is sending me
items.summary: Tristram is back, baby, and the level of detail Blizzard has put into this recreation is genuinely impressive.

content.v: Diablo 4's current Season of Hell's Legacy is focused on celebrating the 30th anniversary of the series, which debuted all the way back in 1997. As part of that effort, Blizzard has been reaching back into the past to bring back iconic characters and enemies like Deckard Cain, Baal, Mephisto, and of course the Big D himself.

The recent discovery of Rune word recipes from Diablo 2 had players wondering if maybe Blizzard has any other blasts from the past stashed away in the new season , and as discovered by redditor JT99-FirstBallot, the answer is a very big yes.

Tristram, of course, is the village that serves as the home base of the original Diablo, where players go to buy and sell items, and interact with a range of sadly doomed NPCs like Griswold, Ogden, Pepin, and Wirt. But it's more than just that: As the hub of what is arguably gaming's most influential action RPG, Tristram is a seminal piece of digital landscape, burned into the memories of old-time Diablo fans—and its destruction sometime prior to the events of Diablo 2 (sorry, mild spoiler there) was a genuine bummer.

What's particularly impressive here is how faithful this recreation of Tristram is. The visuals are obviously dramatically improved (although it looks just as I remember it—isn't the human mind a wonderful thing?) but the layout is spot on, and all the characters are there, doing what they do. What really lands for me, though, is the audio: I'm not a Diablo fan by any stretch these days (I haven't touched the series since Diablo 2) but that Tristram guitar riff hits like a truck, and Griswold's voice, well—that's Griswold's voice!

But the attention to detail runs even deeper. As YouTuber MacroBioBoi explains, this Tristram can be turned into Uber Tristram , a special zone previously only accessible during the Pandemonium Event from the Diablo 2 expansion Lord of Destruction. Uber Tristram is basically a copy of the destroyed village seen in the first act of Diablo 2, with one big expansion: You have to fight Baal, Mephisto, and Diablo at the same time . The payoff for kicking all that Prime Evil ass is the Hellfire Torch , an extremely powerful charm—and yes, the Hellfire Torch reward is waiting for you in Diablo 4 now, too.

Blizzard is clearly going hard to recapture the magic of Diablo's glory days for the 30th anniversary, and going deep too. Which naturally leads to the question: What else is in there? It certainly seems like there's more up the sleeve: The Uber Tristram bosses also drop a new item that players are still trying to figure out what to do with.

Now that Diablo 5 is coming—though not until 2029—there are no more expansions planned for Diablo 4 , and seasons will be the focus. Blizzard says we can expect more storytelling though. Namely, it needs to bring about the apocalyptic return of Diablo to set up the events of the sequel, which will take place after Sanctuary has fallen to the forces of evil .

items.summary: The upcoming 99 Nights in the Forest movie, based on the super-popular Roblox survival-horror game, has report

content.v: The upcoming 99 Nights in the Forest movie, based on the super-popular Roblox survival-horror game, has reportedly brought on a very big name.

According to The Hollywood Reporter , 20th Century Studios--which is owned by Disney--has hired Josh Cooley to write the script. Cooley directed the Oscar-winning Pixar movie Toy Story 4. He also earned an Academy Award nomination for Inside Out. Beyond Disney movies, Cooley directed Transformers One.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/99-Large-1.jpeg

99 Nights in the Forest is developed by Grandma's Favourite Games and exists on the Roblox platform. It remains one of the platform's most popular games , boasting nearly 150,000 players right this moment.
20th Century bought the rights earlier this year following what was reported to have been a "competitive" dealmaking process.

A survival game, 99 Nights in the Forest has players trying to survive for 99 nights in a haunted forest as they fight monsters and save missing children. The developers behind the game–Alec Kieft, Matthew Hufton, and Cameron Angland–will be executive producers for the movie.
20th Century was also behind the Hitman and Assassin's Creed movies, so 99 Nights in the Forest is not the studio's first video game film.
99 Nights in the Forest is also not the first game hosted on Roblox to get a movie deal, as Grow a Garden and Steal a Brainrot also landed Hollywood development deals.

items.title: Activision Calls Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 'The Epic Conclusion,' Leaving Fans Wondering What's Next
items.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is being advertised as the "epic conclusion," suggesting an end of an era for t

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/05/27/cod-mp-preview-br2-1779914695480.jpg
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is being advertised as the "epic conclusion," suggesting an end of an era for the franchise.

In the social copy for the latest trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , Activision stated that the game will be an "epic conclusion" for the Modern Warfare saga. It's unclear if this is the permanent end to the current Modern Warfare universe, or if this is just the end of the ongoing storyline that began back in 2019 with the rebooted Modern Warfare.

Although it's likely just a marketing buzz term, the branding comes at an interesting time. Earlier this week, Treyarch design director Kevin Drew stated that the studio was ready to "make something new and something that nobody's ever experienced before." The comments come as the studio waved goodbye to two back-to-back Black Ops games, with the most recent one being regarded as an underwhelming misfire for the series. The comments led fans to speculate that the Black Ops series may be coming to an end, or at least taking a break, allowing Treyarch to make its first new subfranchise in nearly 20 years.

Some fans are already waving goodbye to the current Modern Warfare series. "Reboot it again," joked one fan in a post on the Call of Duty subreddit . "They should do a COD Ghosts 2 or Infinite Warfare 2, both underrated campaigns," suggested another who may or may not be joking.

If Modern Warfare and Black Ops are truly coming to an end, it will be the first time the series hasn't had at least one existing sub-franchise in the rotation since the creation of Black Ops in 2010. Although we don't know what Sledgehammer Games is working on, it is likely a brand new subfranchise as Advanced Warfare and the studio's subsquent World War II games failed to catch on.

The original Modern Warfare series came to a close after just three games back in 2011. Although the team kicked around ideas for a fourth game back then, they didn't get very far and opted to create something new with Call of Duty: Ghosts.

After Ghosts and Infinity Ward's subsquent game, Infinite Warfare, failed to please fans, the studio went back to old faithful and rebooted Modern Warfare. 2019's effort is largely credited for pulling Call of Duty out of a multi-year rut where fans were beginning to lose faith in the series. It also gave birth to Warzone, the massively popular battle royale mode that has helped carry the series since launch.

During the Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 broadcast, Activision confirmed Death Stranding star Mads Mikkelsen is a major antagonist in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . It's due out on PC and consoles - but not Xbox Game Pass - on October 23.
For more, catch up on everything announced during today's Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 broadcast right here.

items.title: Brandon Sanderson Is Eager to Adapt His Books into a Video Game, Calling Himself a 'Lifelong Gamer'
items.summary: “Lifelong gamer” Brandon Sanderson details his excitement about adapting Mistborn into a video game, explainin

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/17/mistborn-video-game-ign-3-1789650261140.png

During an exclusive interview with IGN, Brandon Sanderson has expressed interest in potentially adapting his Mistborn book series into a video game, but only if he can find the right studio to partner with.
Asked if he'd ever given any thought to a video game adaptation of his work, Sanderson said:
"As a lifelong gamer, suffice it to say that yes, I've thought about this a lot.
"The key will be the right partner. Video games, even the smaller indie games, are huge investments these days.
"Mistborn would almost certainly be the first thing I would try, as the mechanics of the magic and world very naturally lend themselves to such an adaptation – but again, I'd need the right partner."
So it doesn't sound like we'll be getting a Mistborn game anytime soon, but it's certainly on the cards for the distant future after Sanderson's recent comments.

This wouldn't be the first time Mistborn stepped out into other mediums either, with the Mistborn film adaptation in the works after Sanderson recently finished the screenplay ( but also saying there's "still a lot of work to do" ), alongside board games, and the recently released Cosmere RPG tabletop series that's soon getting a Mistborn expansion in November .

Developed by Brotherwise Games in close collaboration with Brandon Sanderson himself, the initial offerings for the Cosmere RPG focus solely on Roshar and the systems of the Stormlight Archive books. Now, Mistborn is joining the ranks with its Handbook, Campaign Guide, and Welcome to Scadriel guide which are all available to preorder now.

It's not a stretch to say that Mistborn could make for an exceptional RPG, akin to something like Baldur's Gate 3 . Moreover, Brotherwise Games has already done much of the groundwork with its impressive tabletop adaptation. There's clearly plenty there that could be built upon or adapted into a video game in the future.

For those who aren’t familiar with Mistborn, the Cosmere or Sanderson’s work in general, the Cosmere is a large galaxy-spanning, progressively more interconnected series of (mostly) epic fantasy novels by Brandon Sanderson. We have a comprehensive reading guide , so to find out more and get a better picture, and I suggest you head there and take a look.

You can read more of the big Brandon Sanderson interview here on IGN, where we've discussed the Wheel of Time cancellation, potentially finishing Game of Thrones , and his current progress on the Mistborn movie.

items.title: Gears Of War: E-Day On PC Won’t Let You Play Without A Ray Tracing-Capable GPU
items.summary: Ahead of its release next month, the official PC specs for Gears of War: E-Day have been revealed. The next ga

content.v: Ahead of its release next month, the official PC specs for Gears of War: E-Day have been revealed. The next game in the series has looked good in recent previews, and if you're aiming to reach a high level of fidelity, you're going to need some fairly chunky PC hardware for 4K gibs and perfect reloads. The good news is that no matter which graphics preset you choose, you'll only need 16GB of RAM--welcome news considering just how much memory costs in the current tech climate.

One thing worth pointing out is that graphics cards without dedicated ray-tracing hardware aren't supported. It's not the first time this has been the case--Indiana Jones and the Great Circle being a prime example--but it does create a hard generational lock for interested players. By making ray-tracing hardware a baseline requirement, the game completely phases out massively popular GPUs like the GTX 1060 or AMD's RX 5000 series, making the RTX 2060 the absolute minimum threshold for playing the new Gears of War.

Developer The Coalition says it has continued to iterate and improve PC stability and performance across a wide range of hardware configurations since July, and if you're aiming to run the game at 1080p and 60fps, you'll need a GPU like an Nvidia GeForce RTX 2060, an entry-level RTX 5050, or an AMD Radeon RX 6600 with 6GB of VRAM. Hitting the 1440p 60fps sweet spot increases the hardware requirements to GPUs with 8GB of VRAM, while running the game at 4K 60fps means you'll need a 12GB GeForce RTX 5070 Ti or an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT.

It's also worth noting that a solid-state drive is required for the game's installation files, and you'll need to free up 115GB of storage space on it. Across the presets, you can expect support for upscaling technology like Nvidia DLSS 4.5, AMD FSR 4, and Intel XeSS 3.0T, which will ease the burden on your PC. The Coalition added that the game includes a benchmark tool to help you fine-tune how it runs on your system.
Gears of War: E-Day PC Requirements

Launching on October 6 for Xbox Series X|S and PC, and day one on Xbox Game Pass, Gears of War: E-Day chronicles the first disastrous encounter between the humans living on the world of Sera and the Locust. The developers behind it recently spoke to GameSpot about a wide range of topics, from solving lore problems to how you strip the flesh off of enemies in the game's new take on Horde mode, and it looks like there's even a Smash Mouth-inspired achievement that you can earn if you want to be a real all-star.

items.title: Valheim devs finally get around to reading 5 years of player feedback, let you remap dodge key
items.summary: Now get to work unlearning five years of three-key muscle memory.

content.v: When battling tree-swinging trolls, ice-spitting dragons, and fire-breathing skeletal demigods, it's hard to think of a skill more important than dodging. A shield or a weapon held up defensively can help, sure, but escaping deadly attacks in Valheim is often down to how quickly you can tuck and roll.

Which makes it a bit curious that over the past five years of early access, you couldn't redbind the dodge skill to a single key or button press. If you want to dodge on keyboard, you have to hold the block button (mouse 2) and press jump (space bar) and pick a direction (WASD). On controller, it's a stick + button combo. No single tap for a deeply important maneuver has been available for the past five years.

Until today! Those busy Valhiem devs finally took a peek at player feedback and noticed the request people have been making constantly for the past five years, seven months, 15 days, 17 hours, and 22 minutes: You have now been granted the ability to remap your dodge key to an alternate—no doubt single-tap—configuration.
Better late than never?

That's not the only key rebinding option that's been added. You can rebind items on the radial wheel and hotbar, too. A much newer request, to disable the intro cinematic (which only appeared with Valheim 1.0 last week), has also been granted. There are also some bug fixes, notably more tinkering with the Valheim cheat -flagging feature that was mislabeling some players and resources as cheats.

Have a look at the full patch notes below, and good luck trying to unlearn the muscle memory you've developed for dodging with three different keys over the past five years or so. One note: the patch, devs say, "will require a few days to get uploaded to all platforms." I've checked and it's live on PC now, however.

items.title: I have officially made Grand Theft Auto 5 good by turning it into a golf sim
items.summary: GTA Tour.

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .

I grew up by a dry riverbed. This was, on the whole, positive, because what a big empty riverbed is good for is setting things on fire, firing air rifles, and walloping golf balls into orbit. Some say they never stopped travelling. They're still out there, somewhere, in the space between the stars.

The reason Grand Theft Auto 5 is worse than a riverbed is that you can't do that last thing. Or, well, you can , but only at officially designated golf courses, which are prisons for the soul. I have now fixed this omission. I installed Street Golf , which lets you play golf, but in the street.

Much like the previous two mods I've bolted onto GTA 5's sagging frame ( LifeInvader Business Mod and Become A Celebrity ), I was immediately impressed by how much of the mod there is. This is no ramshackle creation—the possibility of equipping a golf club and whacking some balls in the street—but comes with a suite of tweakable menus, golf stats, and potent balltypes . Normal balls? Yes. Fire balls? Absolutely. Detonating balls? Very much so. And super balls, which you can set to travel about 200x further than any other ball in your arsenal.

Being as I am now accompanied everywhere by a bodyguard, who is instantly replaced by an almost-identical bodyguard whenever he happens to get pancaked by a flying car or assassinated by a squad of mercenaries, I opted to use him as a kind of ambulatory mini-golf windmill.

My shots were angled towards him, alternately sending him cartwheeling hilariously down the street, sending him cartwheeling even further down the street (super ball, you see), or setting him on fire. The detonating balls never quite worked. The mod procced some sort of achievement when I successfully nailed him in the dome with a maximum-power shot.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/brCBkXmzL5G2pHfZp4A9Pk-1920-80.gif
It's a pleasant distraction. Whenever the travails of my life in Los Santos get too much I can, at any moment, drop into Golf Mode. Would that real life were the same way.

items.title: Epic boss Tim Sweeney says the EU's social media ban for under-13s 'would be terrible for the next generation of humanity'
items.summary: The EU KIDS Act would impose strict new regulations on social media, video sharing, gaming, and other online s

content.v: X Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney says the European Union's plan to restrict social media use by children, including a complete ban for anyone under the age of 13, is "terrible for the next generation of humanity" because of the impact it will have on the growth of creativity and expression.

Announced today, the EU KIDS Act —"Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy," because overwrought acronyms for serious legislation isn't a uniquely American phenomenon—imposes a blanket ban on social media accounts for anyone under the age of 13, although "specially-designed child-friendly video-sharing services" can be established via their parents' or guardian's accounts.

From the ages of 13 to 15, accounts can be set up under the supervision of guardians, although they should have "limited features and screen time." From 15 up, minors can set up their own "autonomous accounts" without parental consent, although "parental guidance remains essential during this stage."

The goal of the new regulations is to effect a "gradual approach" to social media use—the digital equivalent of teaching kids to swim before throwing them into the lake. Notably, the KIDS Act covers not just traditional social media platforms—Instagram, TikTok, and the like—but also "video-sharing platforms, online games, AI chatbots or companions," plus app stores and operating systems. Some services, like online encyclopedias, educational platforms, and digital news outlets, would be exempt.

"Today, our children are engaging with the most sophisticated technologies ever created. Technology that was never created with their wellbeing in mind," EU president Ursula von der Leyen said in a statement . "Our KIDS Act is reversing the burden of proof—it is for platforms to show they are safe by design. And we put parents back in the driving seat, giving them the tools to help their children navigate a safer online world."

Sweeney takes a different view of the situation, however. "This would be terrible for the next generation of humanity," the Epic chief said on X , a day prior to the act's official announcement. "The apps and games of today are the paintbrushes and tree forts of yesterday. Fortnite has Creative Mode, Roblox has Roblox studio, and being a digital creator is in everyone's reach, till politicians take it away."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/jV5vKKRoEmp2n4FtXfm85S-1920-80.png

It's fair to say that it would not be great news for Epic if the EU suddenly made it a whole lot harder for kids under 15 to play Fortnite, and without wanting to sound like an 'in my day we drank straight from the hose!' guy, I would point out that paintbrushes and tree forts are still readily available. It's not as if pre-teens will be reduced to cave painting and hitting each other with rocks if they're suddenly no longer able to generate content for billionaires.

Even so, I find myself on board with Sweeney's broader stance— this isn't a great idea —not out of concerns that it will dull the creative instincts of the next generation, but simply because it's a potential security and privacy nightmare that's difficult to enforce and may or may not achieve its stated goals anyway.

And as other PC Gamer writers have previously pointed out , the impact of social media on young minds is only part of the problem, and arguably a relatively minor part: It also bakes the brains of adults with startling efficiency.

The EU KIDS Act is not a done deal. The proposed regulation has been submitted to the European Parliament and Council, and from there will enter the legislative process required for approval. Given the recent enactment of social media bans for kids and online age verification requirements in Australia , the UK , and some US states , though, and "the clear demand for urgent and comprehensive action" expressed by the EU, I expect it will be soon enough.

items.title: GTA Online Will Be Supported 'Beyond' GTA 6 Release, PC 'Becoming More and More Important'
items.summary: Rockstar Games plans to support GTA Online "beyond" the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, parent company Take-Two

others.title: GTA 6 Boss Says PC Is Becoming “More And More Important”

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/17/gta-6-soundtrack-1789662158949.jpg
Rockstar Games plans to support GTA Online "beyond" the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 , parent company Take-Two has confirmed.

During a recent shareholders meeting (via ResetEra ), Take-Two said "we will continue to support GTA Online after GTA 6 release and beyond." Rockstar had already confirmed that GTA 6 is a single-player only game, so there won't be a multiplayer mode when the game comes out in November. As a result, if you want your online Grand Theft Auto fix, you'll have to divert your attention back to the original iteration of GTA Online.

Presumably there will be another iteration of GTA Online later down the line, but it's becoming increasingly unclear how and when it will be released. Will it be bundled with GTA 6 retroactively? Will it be a standalone game that players have to buy separately?

Twitch boss Dan Clancy, however, is convinced GTA 6 multiplayer will be released in 2027 . In a recent interview with Bloomberg , Clancy said he’d spoken with Rockstar about what the developer has up its sleeve. “We spent a lot of time talking with Rockstar about their plans, and also helping them think about how they can engage our creators,” Clancy said. “You are going to see this big bump with GTA 6, but then an even bigger one next year when they launch multiplayer.”

Meanwhile, during the shareholders meeting, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick responded (via GamesRadar ) to a question about whether the plan for PC had been affected by console shortages, particularly the PS5 Pro.

"The strategy of the company is, over time, generally speaking, to launch for any platforms for which there's a meaningful audience," Zelnick replied, keeping his cards close to his chest. "But that isn't always the case, and certainly, if platforms were no longer viable, we could change that strategy.
"And I would note that the PC platform is becoming more and more important to our company over time."

Zelnick previously said that Rockstar has historically always released its games for consoles first , suggesting a PC version of GTA 6 may follow later. How much later? It's unclear, but GTA 5 remains a massively popular game on the platform.

Ex-Rockstar Games producer John Ricchio stated in an interview earlier this year that the studio's continued decision to skip PC at launch wasn't one rooted in greed . Instead, it was a result of Rockstar wanting to optimize for consoles first and then scaling up for a PC version.

"It's always better to start with the constraints and then extend," said Ricchio. "Because shrinking is a lot harder than extending. It's way harder to make your game performant than it is to just be like 'Oh, we've got extra room? Cool, we can deoptimize or make things more shiny.'"

Could a PC version come alongside the next version of GTA Online? It doesn't seem out of the question if there's going to be a sizable gap. Either way, it's clear that Rockstar is pouring a lot of effort and focus into making GTA 6 the best single-player experience it can be without compromising other parts of the game, even if that means a staggered release of the long-term online money maker.

In related news, Rockstar Games announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album this morning . The soundtrack releases alongside the game on November 19 and features over 30 original songs from major mainstream artists. Six orignal songs from artists like Travis Scott, PinkPantheress, and Morgan Wallen are available to stream on Spotify right now.

items.title: Magic: The Gathering Hobbit Gift Bundles Are Heavily Discounted at Walmart
items.summary: You can save big on a rare MTG Hobbit Gift Bundle at Walmart right now, listed at way under market price.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/17/header-1788811440204-1789661524667.jpg

In case you missed it, Magic: The Gathering has returned to Middle-earth in a big way. The Lord of the Rings set is widely regarded as one of the strongest Universes Beyond releases yet, and The Hobbit is already getting a pretty warm reception from players, too.

The set only launched recently, so its Collector Boosters are proving about as easy to find as the Arkenstone in Smaug's hoard. Thankfully, Walmart has a "deal" that might just be worth hunting down .
We call it a "deal" because, like a lot of things from this set right now, the Magic: The Gathering Hobbit Gift bundle is selling for well above its MSRP at most retailers.

Wizards says the bundle should cost $89.99, making Amazon's $164 price a colossal markup. The same bundle is either considerably more expensive elsewhere or simply sold out, with no clear sign of when it’ll be back.

Walmart, meanwhile, has it for $94.97, sold and shipped directly by Walmart rather than some dodgy third-party seller. Walmart reckons that's "$85.02" in savings, although realistically you're paying just $4.97 more than the original MSRP. Not bad at all when this same bundle can apparently set you back around $200 on TCGplayer.

We're putting all that upfront because you're a big Hobbit now and can spend your money however you please. Just know that this is still an 18% discount compared with what you'd pay for the same bundle elsewhere. If you really want it, go for it. If you don't fancy spending that much, we get it. At least now you know what you're getting into.

So, what's the big draw? While you do get nine Play Boosters in the box, the most valuable cards in the set are exclusive to Collector Boosters. Thankfully, this bundle comes with one of those too, hopefully with a card inside to rule them all.
Smaug? Bard? Gandalf? What’ll it be? Well, that’s the point, really: you could crack open a bunch of neat rare cards, or you could pay next month’s rent by pulling a Gleaming Splendor.

Alongside the ten total packs, you’ll also get 34 land cards, including full-art seasonal Hobbit lands exclusive to this set, plus 10 full-art Middle-earth Journey lands. Honestly, these are so cool I’d probably frame them. There’s also a die included, along with a box to keep everything in.

items.title: Backrooms director & Portal superfan Kane Parsons spotted visiting Valve for the second time this year
items.summary: A well-deserved victory lap, or something more?

content.v: As reported by IGN and Gabe Follower on X , Backrooms director Kane Parsons shared an Instagram story from Valve's Bellevue, Washington headquarters on September 16. The director has previously said that Portal was extremely influential on his work , inspiring hopes for a Parsons-led adaptation or some other collaboration with the studio.

There's more circumstantial evidence in favor of this being more than just a friendly visit: Parsons previously told The New York Times in May that making a Portal feature film would be his "dream." What's more, this isn't the first time Parsons has been seen at Valve HQ. His Instagram story commemorating a visit in June has been preserved by user eugen3 on the Valve subreddit .

Those are encouraging signs that we could have a Portal movie from a guy who'd do a great job on it to look forward to, but there are some caveats. Parsons also told the NYT in May that he doesn't want to move on from Backrooms until it reaches some kind of conclusion, and he is already engaged to direct a sequel for A24.
There is also the matter of J.J. Abrams' seemingly-abandoned Portal movie project. He last spoke about it on the record in 2021, but there could be some standing contracts or agreements to consider.

I find I'm not particularly excited about a videogame adaptation unless the right director's involved, but there's been a lot of that going around recently. Zach Cregger's Resident Evil is looking like a slam dunk , even if some people are grumpy it's not about Leon Kennedy, and I find myself increasingly excited for Alex "The Guy Who Wrote Dredd" Garland's upcoming Elden Ring movie.

Parsons has already shown himself to be a master of the sort of abandoned corporate surrealism that defined Portal⁠, and his passion for the subject matter would also be cause for excitement. Gaming also runs in Parsons' family: His father, Michael Parsons, was a longtime technical artist at Telltale during its legendary 2010s hot streak.

游戏最大的特色是采用了“送外卖”般的金钱奖励机制，非常符合雇佣兵主题的特色，也能够激励玩家不断游玩。在游戏中3个33人小队在地图中建造与战斗，有大小两个地图圈，待在大圈里就可以不断赚钱，待在小圈里则双倍赚钱。游戏里玩家做任何有助于己方的行动都可以赚钱，突击、狙击敌人必然赚钱，开车运物资、开直升机运兵、侦察标记敌人、拿锤子搞基地建设等也都可以赚不少钱。一局游戏通常要快1小时甚至更多，但赚的钱是随时到账的，玩家可以随时退出战局并保留金钱，因此一局游戏中哪方胜利显得不那么重要，重要的是玩得开心并赚钱而归，下次可以买更好的装备再次进游戏。
https://img1b.gamersky.com/users/clubcontent/2026/09/18/origin_1755221_4821738.jpg
https://img1b.gamersky.com/users/clubcontent/2026/09/18/origin_1755221_4821737.jpg
游戏的枪械种类在首发时候还算丰富，模型做得也还不错，枪械后坐力适中，枪感还不错，不过打击感比较一般。目前玩家数量非常多，随时上线都有几十个百人服务器可以加入，亚服延迟都在50左右，玩起来非常丝滑。
https://img1b.gamersky.com/users/clubcontent/2026/09/18/origin_1755221_4821739.jpg

不过本作的成长与匹配机制问题较大，目前战局正在朝越来越混乱且不好玩的方向发展，新玩家除非开黑或有人带，否则进入游戏体验估计较差。游戏的强力武器装备，无论是枪械、载具还是防具，都需要根据级别解锁，游戏里升级速度非常慢，到中后期简直慢到离谱，且等级分为账号等级和兵种等级，玩家除非专精玩一到两个兵种，否则肝度令常人难以接受。新玩家很快就会体验到游戏里玩家间的等级压制，连RPG都没解锁就被机枪悍马、豹2A6坦克追得满地跑，毒刺都没解锁就被Mi-28武直打得抬不起头，没防弹衣拿着MP9微冲在楼里遇到端着M249机枪的重甲怪物等等。
https://img1b.gamersky.com/users/clubcontent/2026/09/18/origin_1755221_4821740.jpg

这些问题的源头，一是上述的等级过肝且装备差异太大，二是游戏没有合理的匹配机制，是类似CS1.5时期的搜索服务器加入的模式，1级玩家和90级玩家在一个服务器里碰到是很正常的。同时，游戏还支持进行中随意换边，这导致了很多令人作呕的事情发生。例如一个玩家拿迫击炮炸了敌人太多次，敌人可以换边过来在基地里TK该玩家泄愤，或者作为内鬼把基地门打开放前队友进来，游戏已经变得混乱不堪。有的战局中玩家遇到队友都愿意冲小圈，小队一起行动体验很好，而在有的战局中如果战友全部各自为战或者只在基地里造墙，则体验非常糟糕。
https://img1b.gamersky.com/users/clubcontent/2026/09/18/origin_1755221_4821741.jpg
https://img1b.gamersky.com/users/clubcontent/2026/09/18/origin_1755221_4821742.jpg
总体来说，这部游戏在开荒时候，大家都在升级，装备差异不大的时候非常有趣。目前正在朝着混乱的方向快速前进，估计在几周后局面就会完全失控，对新人玩家或肝度不够的工作党非常不友好。因此如果有固定队伍开黑，来玩会获得优秀的体验，独狼玩家慎重考虑。
https://img1b.gamersky.com/users/clubcontent/2026/09/18/origin_1755221_4821743.jpg

items.title: MTG Marvel Sets: 4 Crossover Predictions for 2027 and Beyond
items.summary: Explore our predictions for upcoming MTG Marvel sets, including Guardians of the Galaxy, X-Men, Midnight Sons,

content.v: Magic: The Gathering has shown it’s happy to return to planes within the confines of its own universe, but the game’s Universes Beyond sets with Marvel are really only getting started.

Last year’s underwhelming Spider-Man set was followed up by the much more impressive Marvel Super Heroes set in 2026, but we’re expecting many more to come. After two Infinity Stones appeared in those sets, we’re still waiting for another four of them to appear.
Here are our Marvel set predictions for 2027 and beyond. Looking for our wider Universes Beyond predictions? Check out our ideas so far .
Guardians of the Galaxy
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2024/09/05/guardiansofthegalaxy-ep1-1280-1492462186711-160w-1725549802559.jpg
Conspicuous by their absence in the Marvel Super Heroes set are the Guardians of the Galaxy, but given it’s predominantly centered around New York City it’s perhaps not too surprising.
Star-Lord, Gamora, Drax, Rocket, and Groot feel like they could helm a five-color Commander deck, but beyond that, there’s a whole host of cosmic characters we could see.

Beta Ray Bill, Ronan, Gladiator, Nova, Adam Warlock, Nebula, and many more would be great inclusions, but it would also allow for extra printings of Galactus, Silver Surfer, and more. Given Star Trek is coming soon, and Edge of Eternities introduced Spacecraft, expect a card for The Milano.
X-Men and X-Force
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/17/rogue-x-men-1786924882156.png
Yes, we know - some X-Men have been included in the Marvel Super Heroes set, but it’s time for a wider slate of mutants from Xavier’s school and Magneto’s Brotherhood.

It’s likely cards like Wolverine and Storm would see reprints (and maybe fresh designs), but a two-faced card with Jean Grey and the Dark Phoenix, or saga cards for Days of Future Past and more would be awesome.

We’ll take a few more, too, since the likes of Deadpool have been included in Secret Lair drops but aren’t part of the Marvel set. Oh, and Gambit, please, but with an ability that lets you ping a card at your opponent.
Midnight Sons
Marvel has long had a spooky side, and while the Midnight Suns video game remains an underrated gem, the source team, The Midnight Sons, would be an awesome inclusion in Magic form.

Blade, Morbius, Ghost Riders, Man-Thing, Elsa Bloodstone, and even Doctor Strange and Wong could make appearances, and the main roster has included the likes of Scarlet Spider, Iron Fist, and many, many more.
That gives a chance to bring back the horror theming of, say, Duskmourn, reviving mechanics like manifest dread.
Secret Wars
https://assets1.ignimgs.com/2017/11/07/secret-wars-1510015846596.jpg
This could also be another major story moment, but an event set around Secret Wars, which is expected to be the focus of the next big tentpole MCU movie after Doomsday, feels like a given.
The set could include just about anyone transported to Battleworld, teeing up iconic moments that we won’t spoil here in case you’ve not read up on the source material yet.
Secret Wars would be a fitting endcap to the Marvel x MtG crossovers, and you just know we’d get some kind of crazy rare God Emperor Doom card…
What are your predictions? Let us know in the comments!
